svg.aria-label: How to fit, tack and weld the M3 skin section into one rear quarter, in order, with the check that ends each step; repeat on the other side between passes. A side view numbers the joints: the top seam first, then the rear seam, then the front seam, then the lip. The skin seams are butt joints with a 0.8 to 1.0 mm gap, about one skin thickness, over a backing strip of skin-thickness steel plug-welded or bonded to one side only; BMW's own strips are about 60 mm wide, about 30 mm into each side. Step 8, fit: clamps or clecos every 75 to 100 mm; check that every seam is flush within 0.5 mm, the lip is at its target within 3 mm, the door opens and closes and the bumper corner fits. Step 9, tack: the top seam's center, then its ends, then halve the gaps down to a 25 to 30 mm pitch, about 30 tacks; then the rear seam, ends then middle; then the front seam, top, bottom, middle, then halves; check gap, flush, door and templates again and adjust before any stitching. Step 10, the lip: plug welds through 6 mm holes at the factory spot positions, every second position first, from the crown outward, alternately forward and back, then the rest; or bond it and plug every second position. First pass a coupon: each plug 8 to 10 mm across and no more than 3 mm high, tearing a 3 to 8 mm hole when broken. Step 11, stitch: 10 to 15 mm welds between the tacks, in a skip order: gaps 1, 5, 9 on the top seam, then the rear seam's odd gaps, then the front seam's 1, 5, 9, then the other side of the car; later passes 3, 7, 11, then 2, 6, 10, then 4, 8, 12, each only when the area is hand-warm, no more than about 150 mm of weld per seam per pass, until the seam is continuous, as BMW welds its own seams. Check for penetration on the back of every seam and grind and planish each seam as you finish it. After dressing, every template fits within 1 mm, the station offsets match side to side within 3 mm, the body diagonals are within 2 mm of your earlier figures and the door gaps and flush are back.
